title: The Postcard of Bellbird Bay
premise: Lior Coldharbour has spent ten years planning other people's perfect days while hiding from their own, sustained only by unsigned letters that arrive each spring in Bellbird Bay. When the letter-writer — a retired coast guard named Marisol Vane, who once saved Lior's life and never explained why she vanished afterward — moves into the cottage next door, the two are forced to confront the decade of silence between them. As Marisol is drawn back into an old investigation she abandoned to protect someone, Lior must choose between the containable heart they've trained and the whole one being demanded of them. In the end, justice arrives outside any courtroom, Marisol's secret is laid bare, and Lior plans one last wedding: their own.
about_author: Astrid Ishikawa is a former event coordinator who spent six years watching strangers promise each other forever before writing it down instead. She lives on a windswept peninsula with her partner and an opinionated kelpie named Postscript.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Opening on the wedding of the season, Lior narrates their philosophy of the heart as a trainable muscle while flawlessly executing a ceremony they feel nothing at. A tenth anonymous letter arrives, postmarked Bellbird Bay, and for the first time it includes a return address. Emotional beat: controlled detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Cottage Next Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A moving truck appears beside Lior's rented cottage, and out steps Marisol Vane — older, weathered, unmistakably the handwriting Lior knows by heart. Their first conversation is all deflection and salt air, both pretending not to recognize what the other means. Emotional beat: shock masked as politeness, old grief stirring.

chapters.title: Ten Springs of Ink
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Through her eyes we learn she wrote every letter from a lighthouse station up the coast, watching over Lior without permission after the accident neither of them names. She moved here because the past finally caught up: someone is asking questions about the night she pulled Lior from the water. Emotional beat: guilt braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A storm strands the two neighbors together, and Marisol admits she was the coast guard on duty the night Lior's brother drowned — and that she saved Lior instead when she could only reach one. The letters were penance. Lior walks out into the rain. Emotional beat: betrayal and relief arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Isn't
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Back at work, Lior sabotages their own composure, snapping at clients whose joy feels obscene now. A wealthy groom turns out to be connected to the man Marisol has been hiding from — Harlan Reeve, who caused the accident and bought his way free. Emotional beat: professional armor failing, purpose rekindling.

chapters.title: Harlan Reeve's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She reveals the full case she abandoned: evidence that Reeve's negligence killed three people, buried by money and fear, including testimony she withdrew to keep Lior safe from his retaliation. Now Reeve has found her again. Lior, furious and awake, refuses to be protected anymore. Emotional beat: protection reframed as another kind of cage.

chapters.title: Pieces on Loan
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The pair works together by lamplight, rebuilding the case from Marisol's hidden records while dancing around everything unsaid. Lior realizes they've been lending pieces of their heart for years — to clients, to letters — never the whole. A near-kiss breaks off when a car slows outside. Emotional beat: intimacy sharpened by danger.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Reeve confronts Marisol directly, offering hush money and threatening to expose how she falsified the rescue log that night. She must decide whether survival was worth a decade of silence. Meanwhile Lior discovers the falsified log alone and feels the ground shift again. Emotional beat: shame meeting its limit; love demanding honesty over safety.

chapters.title: Bellbird Bay Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax. At the Reeve wedding Lior is hired to run, they turn the toast hour into testimony: survivors' statements, the ledger, the log, broadcast before the town and a journalist planted among the guests. Reeve's empire cracks publicly; Marisol surrenders herself for the falsified record on the courthouse steps, hand in Lior's hand. Emotional beat: justice seized, cost accepted, no more hiding.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, months later. Marisol returns from her reduced sentence to a repaired cottage and a town that finally knows the truth. Lior, who swore off believing in weddings, has planned one anyway — small, imperfect, theirs — and reads aloud the eleventh letter, signed at last with both their names. Emotional beat: the contained heart given away entire, and surviving it.
